user.title: Connect to Rover
user.description:
Rover has no public API and its sign-in page is behind a bot check, so this integration reuses a session from a browser where you are already signed in.

1. Sign in at rover.com in your browser.
2. Open developer tools (F12) and go to the **Network** tab.
3. Reload the page and click any request to rover.com.
4. Under **Request Headers**, right-click the `Cookie` row and copy its value.
5. Paste it below.

A valid value is a long list of `name=value` pairs separated by `; ` - not a single cookie. Redacted example:

`__cf_bm=aaaaaaaa...; csrftoken=bbbbbbbb...; sessionid=cccccccc...; roverid=dddddddd...`

A `document.cookie` value from the browser console works too, and a leading `Cookie:` is fine - both are cleaned up for you.

The cookie is stored in Home Assistant's config entry, not in your YAML, and is redacted from diagnostics. It expires after a few weeks, and Home Assistant will ask you for a new one when it does.

data_description.cookie: The whole Cookie header value, with every `name=value` pair - usually several hundred characters long.

reauth_confirm.title: Rover session expired
reauth_confirm.description:
The saved Rover session is no longer accepted. Copy a fresh `Cookie:` header from a browser where you are signed in to Rover, using the same steps as when you set this up.

Your entities, history and automations are kept - only the saved session is replaced.

data_description.cookie: The whole Cookie header value, with every `name=value` pair.

error.invalid_auth: Rover accepted the request but reported no signed-in session. The cookie looks like a whole header, so the likely cause is that the browser you copied it from has since signed out. Sign in to Rover again, copy a fresh header and retry.
error.partial_cookie: That is a single cookie, not a whole Cookie header. It needs every `name=value` pair from the header, separated by `; ` - copying one row out of the Application (or Storage) cookie table is not enough. Use the Network tab, click a request to rover.com, and copy the whole value of the `Cookie` request header.
error.invalid_cookie_format: That does not look like a Cookie header. It should be a list of `name=value` pairs separated by `; `, for example `csrftoken=abcd1234; sessionid=efgh5678`.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Rover. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.blocked: Rover answered with a bot-protection challenge rather than data. This usually clears by itself - wait a few minutes and try again.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: Rover is already set up. This integration supports one Rover account per Home Assistant.

init.title: Rover options
init.description:
How often to poll Rover for new conversations.

Six hours is the default, and lowering it is not a free win: the endpoint this integration reads sits behind bot protection, and frequent polling from an authenticated session is what gets an IP flagged - after which the integration reports `Blocked` and returns nothing at all. Bookings change on the order of days, so a long interval loses nothing. One hour is the shortest allowed.

data_description.scan_interval_hours: Hours between polls. Between 1 and 168 (a week); the default is 6.

blocked_repeatedly.title: Rover is refusing automated requests
blocked_repeatedly.description:
Rover has answered {title} with a bot-protection challenge instead of data {polls} polls in a row, so bookings have stopped updating. `sensor.rover_session` reports `Blocked` and the other sensors are unavailable.

Your saved session is probably fine - this is Rover's protection reacting to the request, not to the cookie, so there is nothing to re-paste.

What helps:

- Wait. Challenges usually clear on their own.
- Check the poll interval under **Settings > Devices & services > Rover Client > Configure**. If it was shortened, put it back up; frequent polling is what attracts this.
- Open rover.com in a browser on the same network and complete any challenge it shows you there.

This notice disappears by itself as soon as a poll gets through.
